title: Add opt-in default-browser links for web apps
head: 06b2e28179d6
workflow: Opus full review, Sol boundary hunter, Opus self-check of the draft, editorial check, batch gates

leads.summary: A failed default-browser process can make the host claim success and discard the link
leads.consequence: With a registered HTTP(S) desktop handler whose Exec program exists but exits nonzero, shipped xdg-utils 1.2.1 unconditionally exits 0 after running it. The host replies opened=true. A captured click is prevented with no fallback, or a target=_blank popup is closed, losing navigation rather than keeping it in Chromium. Repeating the click has the same effect until the handler is fixed. The test mocks subprocess.run(returncode=1), which cannot model this actual xdg-open exit.
leads.triage: already in Opus F1 (case C); corroboration

leads.summary: Line-based rewriting changes unrelated browser arguments in a valid inline flags line
leads.consequence: Arch's shipped Chromium launcher splits each flags-file line into multiple shell-style arguments. Given a valid line '--load-extension=/keep --user-data-dir=/profile', enabling writes '--load-extension=/keep --user-data-dir=/profile,/path/to/webapp-links'. Chromium still receives the original /keep extension, but its --user-data-dir now points at a different profile path; users appear to have lost their session/settings, and the intended extension does not load. The command exits 0, touches the enabled marker and prints success. Disabling later removes the suffix and restores the original profile string. The same assumption fails for quoted load-extension arguments and inline comments. Parse argument boundaries as the actual launcher does rather than treating a line as a single list.
leads.triage: factual, coordinator verified chromium-launcher v8 launcher.c:47-55 g_shell_parse_argv per line and toggle Python; Opus self-check reproduced; published as low note (default file is one flag per line)

leads.summary: Re-enabling after PR #12971 defeats its Chrome safety migration and fails its install test
leads.consequence: Open PR #12971 intentionally omits --load-extension from Chrome 137+ flag files and migrates existing chrome/google-chrome files to remove it. The combined installer merges textually without conflict, but with webapp-links enabled it immediately re-adds that flag, prints #12971's warning that Chrome cannot load unpacked extensions, and its assertion that Chrome flags omit the switch fails. Separate open PR #7817 packages only copy-url, yt-dlp and whatsapp-slim as signed Chrome CRXs, excluding this fourth extension. Both independent PRs report Google-branded Chrome ignores --load-extension; browser-level proof should be checked against Chromium/Chrome code before publicly asserting that branded Chrome cannot load it. At minimum integrate with whichever Chrome installation policy merges and update its test and warning.
leads.triage: factual, coordinator verified #12971 open and its diff; toggle on re-adds line after its sed; published, narrowed (stock #12971 test does not fail by itself)

leads.summary: A nondefault XDG_CONFIG_HOME makes the toggle edit a different file than Chromium reads
leads.consequence: The Arch Chromium launcher reads $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/chromium-flags.conf when the variable is set, but this option edits only $HOME/.config/chromium-flags.conf. For a user with XDG_CONFIG_HOME elsewhere, enabling reports success and writes the marker but does not load the extension from their actual flags. Disabling and refresh continue to target the wrong file. Native host manifests are also installed only below $HOME/.config, so must be aligned with each browser's actual config root. A normal XDG_CONFIG_HOME unset account works as the positive control.
leads.triage: factual but consistent with existing Omarchy ~/.config convention; not published

leads.summary: Python's IDNA2003 normalization disagrees with browser origins for internationalized hosts
leads.consequence: The documented allowlist accepts Unicode HTTP(S) origins. With an app at https://faß.de and an allowed identity origin, Python maps its config key to https://fass.de, while browser URL.origin is https://xn--fa-hia.de. Both JS policy and host therefore fail to associate the actual app with its group, routing an intended in-app sign-in click externally. Worse, it can apply the group to the distinct https://fass.de app instead. Use the browser's canonical ASCII origin semantics or require/configure punycode and reject ambiguous Unicode entries.
leads.triage: plausible, niche (deviation characters only); not published

leads.summary: The new host repeats a proven unsafe sed substitution for development checkout paths
leads.consequence: With a valid OMARCHY_PATH containing '&', sed expands the matched placeholder in the replacement, producing a JSON path different from the executable. Quotation marks or backslashes can corrupt JSON, and '|' can cause the installer to fail. The toggle can still mark itself enabled and append flags for the ampersand case, but Chromium cannot start the host; clicked links stay inside the app. The host template needs proper JSON string encoding, e.g. jq --arg .path, matching open PR #12384's fix for sibling hosts.
leads.triage: pattern copied from sibling installers, open PR #12384 addresses siblings; not published

leads.summary: The toggle advertises Opera, Vivaldi and Helium flag files without corresponding native-host registrations
leads.consequence: If one of the named browsers loads the extension from the edited flag file, it cannot reach com.omarchy.webapp_links: no manifest is installed in the Opera, Vivaldi or Helium config roots. Its policy lookup fails, so clicks are left in the app despite toggle reporting success. Either drop these unsupported flag files from the toggle or register (and remove) the host in their actual profile roots. Open Helium/Vivaldi installer PRs #8801/#12132 and #9430/#12754 make this omission more likely to affect supported users; confirmation that each branded browser honors the unpacked-extension switch remains needed.

leads.summary: Canonical-equivalent allowlist keys silently overwrite earlier groups
leads.consequence: A valid JSON config with distinct keys https://app.example.com and https://app.example.com:443 normalizes both to the same origin; the second group's members overwrite the first. An earlier configured login origin silently ceases to be allowed, so its clicked sign-in link is sent to the default browser. Reject duplicate normalized keys with a config error, or union member sets, rather than discarding entries.

leads.summary: New fixture cannot catch replacing the opener-frame origin with the top-frame origin
leads.consequence: A plausible regression in background.js replacing source.url with app.url would leave every new popup assertion green, because executeScript's mock returns the same source URL for every requested frame. In a popup from a cross-origin embedded auth iframe, this would route based on the wrong origin. Add a case whose frame 0 and frame 5 URLs differ, then assert the forwarded native message.source and the routing decision.
leads.triage: already in Opus F4 / Q4; published as one sentence in the frame finding

leads.summary: New lifecycle test never exercises the changed install or refresh entry points
leads.consequence: The test claims browser-config replacement restores opt-in but manually runs the standalone toggle after the cp. Removing both PR-added calls to omarchy-toggle-webapp-links from omarchy-install-browser and omarchy-refresh-chromium would not change the test's assertions. Test those entry points with an existing marker and verify the resulting flags/host; the existing default-apps-test runs only with opt-in off.

leads.summary: Hypothesis: Google-branded Chrome ignores the only extension installation method used here
leads.consequence: Two related open PRs report Chrome 137+ unconditionally rejects --load-extension. If that shipped-browser premise holds, enabling the option for Chrome merely writes a dead flag and host file, without installing the extension at all. This is separate from the verified #12971 merge/test conflict. Settle by reading the Chrome 137+/151 command-line load-extension gate in the branded browser's upstream source, or by a permitted isolated Chrome profile fixture; neither is provided in this hunt.
leads.triage: settled by Opus F3 from Chromium source; published

leads.summary: Hypothesis: the popup gate needs a browser-level check across app window modes and opener frames
leads.consequence: The only popup coverage supplies invented webNavigation fields and scripted frame results. This does not establish whether installed PWA --app-id windows, standalone --app windows, or branded browsers actually report display-mode standalone and an injectable sourceFrameId as required. A mismatch would leave a popup in the app, or close a window after routing based on an incorrect opener. Read the shipped Chromium browser core's webNavigation event source, scripting results, display-mode implementation, and each named browser difference, or run an authorized headed browser fixture; no assertion of actual browser failure is made here.
leads.triage: covered by Opus Q3 and the disclosed limit; not published separately

flags.claim: users with Firefox or Zen ... see no response for 10 s on the first external click after starting a session
flags.why: The trigger is that the default browser is not running when the link is handed off, not session start. It happens on any click while that browser is closed (for example the first one after login, or after the user quits it), and never if the user already has it open. After the timeout the browser keeps running, so later clicks are fine until it is closed again.

flags.claim: The page then appears in both browsers, and the app window has left its own page.
flags.why: Lost qualifier. 'The app window has left its own page' applies to same-tab clicks (links.js line 23 location.assign). For target=_blank or window.open, the app stays put and the Chromium tab is kept instead (background.js line 39). The table row above states both cases correctly.

flags.claim: Disabling restores the flag files byte for byte.
flags.why: Holds for the tested files, which all end with a newline. A flag file without a trailing newline and without a --load-extension line gains a newline when enabled, and disabling keeps it: 24 bytes before, 25 after on then off. Files with a line holding several flags or one-flag-per-line files were restored exactly.

flags.claim: allowlist groups keyed by the app do not apply to popups from frames. ... it keeps sign-in popups opened from a provider's iframe in the app.
flags.why: The host's related() check (bin/omarchy-chromium-webapp-links-host lines 64-66, 86) matches when both the frame's origin and the destination are in one group. So a group does apply to a frame popup when the frame's origin is itself listed; what does not carry over is the app's own membership (an app-to-login entry does not cover widget-to-login). My final report F4 has the same overstatement. Also, a same-origin popup from a provider iframe is not routed, so it stays in Chromium (a Chromium window or tab), not strictly 'in the app'; this is inferred from code, not tested with a real provider. Line 48 ('is routed ... although that is the app's own origin') likewise holds unless the widget's origin and the app share a group.

flags.claim: an app page's own a.click() calls open default-browser tabs without user action ... so the page's own click handlers on cross-origin links never run
flags.why: Scope too broad. links.js lines 11-17 only intercept (and stop propagation for) anchors in a standalone window whose target is empty or _self, without a download attribute, after the policy has loaded, and whose origin is not allowlisted. Cross-origin target=_blank links and allowlisted links still reach page handlers. The a.click() effect has the same conditions.

flags.claim: accepts only HTTP(S) URLs without credentials, whitespace, control characters or backslashes
flags.why: Nitpick. The host rejects characters with ord <= 32 (space and C0 controls) and backslash; DEL (0x7f) and non-ASCII control characters are not rejected. Negligible impact: Chromium serialises hrefs with percent-encoding and the URL goes to xdg-open as an argument without a shell.

flags.claim: source review of the pinned head 06b2e28, plus xdg-utils 1.2.1, Chromium and AUR launcher sources
flags.why: Nitpick attribution. The 'Lines with several flags' note relies on Arch's official chromium package launcher (foutrelis/chromium-launcher v8), which is not an AUR package. The AUR sources are the Chrome, Brave and Edge wrappers.

flags.claim: sandbox run of a three-way merge with the option enabled; 'a three-way merge with #12971 ran in an isolated sandbox'
flags.why: Not part of my evidence; I did not run a merge. The logic is CORRECT from the diffs: #12971's copy_chromium_flags writes chrome-flags.conf with sed '/^--load-extension=/d'. This PR's copy_chromium_flags then runs omarchy-toggle-webapp-links on when the toggle is enabled, and with no --load-extension line the toggle appends '--load-extension=<webapp-links path>' (toggle Python lines 73-75). Nuance: the re-added line holds only the webapp-links path, not the bundled extensions #12971 removed. The refresh path would also re-add it, because the toggle edits chrome-flags.conf whenever it exists.

flags.claim: nothing in the extension stops or pauses its navigation, which Chromium starts right away
flags.why: 'which Chromium starts right away' is an inference, not verified in Chromium source or a browser. The draft's line 32 qualifier ('follows from the order of calls in the source; the double request was not measured') covers the conclusion, so this is acceptable if that qualifier stays.

flags.claim: Opus 5.5 Xhigh technical review and final fact check
flags.why: I cannot observe my own model or effort setting; the coordinator verifies this from the subagent transcripts.

issues.requirement: Substantive findings need a descriptive heading, observed behavior, **Impact** and **Suggested change** as separate elements (Delivered comment structure item 2; Editorial compliance gate).
issues.excerpt: ### Google Chrome does not load `--load-extension` ... so for those users the toggle edits `chrome-flags.conf`, registers the host and prints "enabled", but nothing changes. ... **Suggested change:** drop Chrome from the documented browsers ...
issues.correction: Add a separate **Impact:** paragraph to this finding. The impact is currently embedded in the observed-behavior prose. Move the existing statement there without adding new technical claims, for example: users whose default browser is Google Chrome see the toggle report "enabled", but links are not routed, and the manual and the test's pass message name Chrome. Keep the observed behavior, the PR #12971 interaction note and the Suggested change as they are.

comment:
## Automated AI review

> **Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review.

**Verified:** the toggle, flag-file editing, native host registration, command routing, refresh and disable work as described for Chromium, and the native host's input validation is sound. The main issue is how the hand-off to the default browser is judged: `xdg-open`'s exit status and duration do not tell the host whether the link opened, so a cold-started default browser leads to a 10 s pause and the link opening in both browsers. Google Chrome also does not load command-line extensions, so the documented Chrome support does not take effect.

### A cold-started default browser opens the link twice, after a 10 s pause

On Hyprland, `xdg-open` 1.2.1 (the version Arch ships) finds no known desktop and takes its generic path. That path runs the default `x-scheme-handler/https` handler **in the foreground** and then exits 0 whatever the handler returned (`scripts/xdg-open.in`, `search_desktop_file`: `env "$command" "$@"` followed by `exit_success`). When Firefox is not already running, that foreground process is the browser itself, so `subprocess.run(..., timeout=10)` in `bin/omarchy-chromium-webapp-links-host` times out.

Sandbox run: the PR's real host, driven like Chromium with length-prefixed stdin, the real `xdg-open` 1.2.1, `XDG_CURRENT_DESKTOP=Hyprland`, and a fake default browser registered in `mimeapps.list`:

| Fake default browser | Host reply | Time | Result in the extension |
|---|---|---|---|
| exits 0 at once (browser already running) | `opened: true` | 0.07 s | correct |
| stays in the foreground (browser not yet running) | `opened: false` | 10.03 s | the link opens in the default browser **and** the app window navigates to it (`links.js` `location.assign`), or the popup tab is kept |
| exits 1 (browser command fails) | `opened: true` | 0.06 s | the click was cancelled or the popup closed, so **nothing opens** |
| no handler, all fallback browsers fail (control) | `opened: false` | 0.09 s | correct fallback |

In the second row, the fake browser had received the URL and was still running when the host replied.

**Impact:** users with Firefox or Zen as their default browser, the audience for this option, see no response for 10 s when they click an external link while that browser is not running (for example the first click after login). The page then appears in both browsers: a clicked link also navigates the app window away from its page, and a popup keeps its Chromium tab. The third row contradicts the manual's "If the native host or default browser is unavailable, links remain navigable in Chromium."

**Suggested change:** start the default browser detached and do not wait for it to exit, for example with `subprocess.Popen(..., start_new_session=True)` or through `systemd-run --user`, which `omarchy-launch-browser` uses. Treat a successful start as the hand-off, not `xdg-open`'s exit status.

Not tested with a real Firefox on a desktop; the browser was a stub.

### New-window targets load in Chromium before the extension closes them

`background.js` handles `webNavigation.onCreatedNavigationTarget`, then waits for `scripting.executeScript` in the opener and for the native host to run `xdg-open`, and only then calls `chrome.tabs.remove(details.tabId)`. That event only reports the new tab; nothing in the extension stops or pauses its navigation, which Chromium starts right away.

**Impact:** for `target=_blank` links and `window.open`, the destination is normally requested first by Chromium, with the Chromium profile's cookies, and then again by the default browser. A single-use link opened from a mail or chat web app (email verification, magic sign-in, password reset, one-click unsubscribe) can be used up by the discarded Chromium tab. A Chromium tab also briefly appears. This follows from the order of calls in the source; the double request was not measured in a real browser.

**Suggested change:** document the double load, or intercept new-window targets in a way that stops them before their request is sent.

### Google Chrome does not load `--load-extension`

Current Chromium source ignores the switch in Google Chrome builds (`chrome/browser/extensions/extension_service.cc`: "`--load-extension is not allowed in Google Chrome, ignoring.`", unconditional since commit `04f6233ce5be`, 2025-09-25). `bin/omarchy-launch-webapp` runs web apps in Chrome when Chrome is the default browser.

**Impact:** for users whose default browser is Google Chrome, the toggle edits `chrome-flags.conf`, registers the host and prints "enabled", but links are not routed. The manual and the test's pass message name Chrome.

The related open PR #12971 removes `--load-extension` from Chrome flag files for this reason. If both merge and this option is on, `omarchy-install-browser chrome` writes the flag file without the line and then this PR's toggle call adds it back (sandbox run of a three-way merge with the option enabled).

**Suggested change:** drop Chrome from the documented browsers and from the toggle's flag files, or state that Google Chrome does not load command-line extensions. Edge's handling was not verified.

### Popups from embedded frames are judged by the frame's origin, not the app's

`background.js` compares the destination with the URL of `details.sourceFrameId` and uses frame 0 only for the standalone check. In a mocked run of the PR's `background.js`:
- A YouTube embed in `https://app.example.com` opening `https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=x` stays in a Chromium tab.
- A `https://widget.example.org` iframe opening `https://app.example.com/settings` is routed to the default browser, although that is the app's own origin.

**Impact:** the manual describes behaviour relative to the app ("Other origins ... open in your default browser unless you allow them for that app"), but for popups from frames an allowlist group applies only if it lists the frame's origin: an app-to-login entry does not cover a popup from a widget iframe to the same login page. The current choice may be partly intended, since a same-origin popup opened from a provider's iframe stays in Chromium without configuration (inferred from the code, not tested with a real provider).

**Suggested change:** decide which origin applies and document it. Frame 0's URL is already fetched if app-relative behaviour is wanted. The test's popup mock returns the same URL for every frame, so it does not cover either choice.

### Smaller notes

- **Script clicks and page handlers.** `links.js` has no `event.isTrusted` check, so an app page's own `a.click()` calls open default-browser tabs without user action. The listener captures at `document` from `document_start` and calls `stopImmediatePropagation()`, so the page's own click handlers never run for the cross-origin links it routes (same-tab, non-download, not allowlisted), for example share buttons or confirmation prompts. Suggested change: `if (!event.isTrusted) return;`, and consider whether to run after the page's handlers.
- **Fullscreen.** Chromium reports `display-mode: fullscreen` rather than `standalone` for a fullscreen app window (`browser_web_contents_delegate.cc` checks fullscreen before the app-window branch). Routing is therefore off in fullscreen, and a page loaded while fullscreen never requests the policy. Whether Hyprland's fullscreen sets Chromium's fullscreen state was not tested.
- **Flag-file list.** The toggle edits `opera-`, `vivaldi-` and `helium-flags.conf` but registers no host for those browsers. It edits `google-chrome-beta-` and `google-chrome-unstable-flags.conf`, which the AUR wrappers do not read (they read `chrome-beta-` and `chrome-dev-flags.conf`). It also registers hosts for Brave Beta and Nightly without editing `brave-beta-` or `brave-nightly-flags.conf`. The files Omarchy's installer creates are all covered.
- **Lines with several flags.** Arch's Chromium launcher shell-parses each line, so `--load-extension=/a --user-data-dir=/p` is valid. The toggle treats everything after `--load-extension=` as one comma list and would append the extension to the profile path instead. Omarchy's default file has one flag per line, so this only affects hand-edited files.
- **Service worker filename.** `copy-url/background-4.js` has a comment saying Chromium caches service workers of `--load-extension` extensions, which is why that filename carries a version. `webapp-links/background.js` does not, so later changes may not reach existing users. This relies on the repository's own comment.
- **Manual heading.** The new `## Included web apps` holds one sentence, followed by sibling `## HEY`, `## Basecamp` and other headings.
- **Related open PR:** #11631 ("Open web app links in the default browser") routes new targets from app windows through the Copy URL extension and `omarchy-launch-browser`. With both merged and this option on, one popup could be handled by both extensions.

**Verified:** `omarchy toggle webapp-links on` routes to the new command. Enabling twice adds the extension once and keeps other extensions and flags. Disabling restores the tested flag files byte for byte. `omarchy-refresh-chromium` reapplies the option, and `omarchy commands --check` passes. The native host bounds the message size, requires a JSON object, accepts only HTTP(S) URLs without credentials, spaces, ASCII control characters below 0x20 or backslashes, and passes the URL to `xdg-open` as an argument without a shell. The PR's test passes, and two mutated copies (one without `stopImmediatePropagation`, one keeping `BROWSER`) make it fail.

---

## Review information

**Test scope:** source review of the pinned head `06b2e28`, plus xdg-utils 1.2.1, Chromium, and Arch and AUR launcher sources. The PR test, mutation checks, the native host with the real `xdg-open` and a stub browser, mocked extension scripts and a three-way merge with #12971 ran in an isolated sandbox with a synthetic home. No real browser, desktop session or default-browser launch was used, so the double request, fullscreen behaviour and Edge and Brave handling of `--load-extension` are untested.

**AI process:** Opus 5.5 Medium coordination and synthesis, Opus 5.5 Xhigh technical review and final fact check, GPT 6 Sol Xhigh search for related issues, Opus 5.5 Medium editorial check.

**Opt out:** To stop receiving these reviews, reply to this comment saying so.
